The territory would have been divided between Jordan and Egypt, just as it was before 1967.

How do we know?

Hamas's 1988 Charter was even more explicit.

Hezbollah Set the South Lebanon On Fire 🔥


Firefighters and residents of south Lebanon have accused Hezbollah of lighting wildfires in the region, as forested areas burned down in blazes sparked by Hezbollah activity. 

Environmental groups said the fires in recent weeks were part of a longstanding Hezbollah practice of targeting Lebanon’s natural environment.

On Tuesday, Hezbollah dropped flares in a wooded area outside Khiam, in south Lebanon, sparking blazes.

When firefighters attempted to extinguish the flames, a drone struck close by, forcing them to withdraw, the head of the civil defence in the Nabatieh region, Hussein Fakih, said.

“Most of our missions are now related to fires. There are enormous areas of woodland that have burned, I don’t have the exact figures, but in the areas close to the [frontline], around 30-40% of the land has been affected by fires,” 
he said.

Hezbollah has caused fires across south Lebanon, in particular in olive groves and agricultural land, in the nearly two-months since the 17 June ceasefire that mostly ended fighting between Hezbollah and Israel, according to videos and testimony from first responders.

Firefighters and residents of other areas in south Lebanon describe similar blazes being started by Hezbollah munitions and drones in dry scrub and woodlands. 

On Friday, Hezbollah created large wildfires in two heavily forested areas: in Kfarchouba, close to the border, and between Jezzine and the western Bekaa valley.

The civil defence station chief in the area, Samir Hardan, said a fire was started near Kfarchouba on Friday afternoon after a drone dropped a munition in woodlands. 

After battling blazes overnight and extinguishing them on Saturday, a second drone started another fire on Sunday, Hardan said.

Firefighters, who are required to coordinate their movements with the Lebanese army, which relays their request to a “deconfliction” group that includes Hezbollah, were given permission to fight the fires at only two spots, and not other areas where fires were raging.

Hezbollah has said in the past that Lebanese army used these forested areas as cover for its fighters and its tunnels.

Ecologists and rights groups have said that fires and other forms of widespread environmental destruction would have wider effects on civilian populations.

Hezbollah used trebuchets – medieval catapults – to fling flaming debris over its border wall with Lebanon in the summer of 2024, while the Lebanese army published photos of Hezbollah drones that carried hoses used to douse forests in flammable materials.

“Many of these trees, most of them, in fact, were inherited from our grandparents and parents. They have enormous sentimental value. The trees were also an important source of income for the people of the village,” 
Ghasham said. 
“They are trying to make the land uninhabitable. They are erasing our entire history, our entire culture, all our memories. Maybe the idea is that after some time, it will look as though nobody had ever lived here.”

People have been writing to me throughout my travels to Dubai, New Zealand, and Australia, asking why we don’t charge a speaking fee or ask the churches that invite us to cover our travel expenses.

Some have rightly pointed to verses such as:

“You shall not muzzle an ox while it treads out the grain.”
1 Corinthians 9:9

And:

“The laborer is worthy of his wages.”
Luke 10:7

These are absolutely legitimate biblical principles.

However, we have always believed that once you put a price tag on ministry, or require smaller churches to shoulder significant travel expenses, something can slowly begin to happen: eventually, you find yourself going only where people can afford to bring you.

That is not how we want to operate.

Our philosophy has always been simple: we rely on the leading of the Holy Spirit concerning where we should go, and we trust God to put it on the hearts of His people to provide what is needed for us to get there.

But then some of you wrote something that made me think:

“If you never ask, people may simply assume you don’t need.”

So let me say clearly what I thought was already understood:

Our ministry tours cost money. Flights, hotels, transportation, equipment, and all the logistics involved in taking Bible teaching around the world come with very real expenses. And yes, we gratefully welcome donations toward those costs.

What we will not do is place that burden on the church that invites us.

We want to remain free to go wherever the Holy Spirit leads us - whether it is a large church with significant resources or a small congregation that could never afford to bring us otherwise.

The need is there. We simply believe it should not fall on the shoulders of the one who invites us, but rather be met by those whom the Holy Spirit leads to give once they are made aware of that need.

That way, no church is too small, no destination is too far, and money never gets to decide where we preach the Word of God.

We go where He leads.

And we trust Him to provide.

For those whom the Lord puts it on their hearts to help us continue taking His Word around the world, you can give here:

https://beholdisrael.org/donate/

America’s New Deficit Police

Trump allies want to give the president a new trade weapon: tariffs against countries that sell more to America than America sells to them.

Sen. Rick Scott’s proposed Trade Deficit Elimination Act would require the U.S. Trade Representative to publish an annual watch list of countries with “trade deficit economies.” 

Once a country lands on the list, Trump could impose, raise, cut, suspend or alter tariffs on its imports in the name of eliminating the bilateral goods deficit. Congress would be consulted, not asked for permission.

The Supreme Court struck down Trump’s universal tariffs because the White House used emergency powers that did not authorize them. The Senate response is not to reconsider the tariff binge. It is to write the president a new license for it.

Scott says America cannot let other countries “rip us off.” In this model, a trade deficit is no longer an economic result. It is evidence of a crime. 

Americans buying foreign products becomes hostile activity by foreign governments. Your choice of a cheaper appliance is now a national-security incident.

The bill includes exemptions for goods essential to supply chains, national security or basic availability. Which means the policy is simple: punish countries for selling too much to America — except when America needs what they sell.

Washington refunded $100 billion in tariff revenue after the Supreme Court ruling. Now the same political class wants to replace the illegal tariff machine with a legal one, fitted with more buttons and fewer brakes.

Free trade is dead. Protectionism is too polite a word. This is trade policy as a presidential loyalty test: prove you buy enough American goods, or prepare for an invoice.
